title: Ensure 'Show Status Bar' is not 'Hidden'
description: This setting controls whether mousing over a link displays the full URL that the link will follow. Rationale: Showing the full URL allows users to validate that a link is performing the action it claims, and may prevent users from following malicious links. Audit reads ShowOverlayStatusBar from the com.apple.Safari preference domain of the account running the scan (the PDF checks the same token in com.apple.Safari.plist; manual check: Follow the below steps and verify that Show Status Bar is not 'Hidden`: 1. Click View. 2. Verify Hide Status bar is displayed.). Safari is sandboxed, so the reading process needs Full Disk Access on macOS 10.14+. A missing key exits non-zero and is reported as FAIL even where the built-in default is compliant. Values forced by a configuration profile live in /Library/Managed Preferences and are not read here.
reference: CIS macOS Safari Benchmark v2.0.0 - 11.1 Ensure 'Show Status Bar' is not 'Hidden'

audit.command: out=$(defaults read com.apple.Safari ShowOverlayStatusBar 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.guidance: Follow the below steps to set Show Status Bar: 1. Click View. 2. Click Show Status Bar. Or deploy a configuration profile for com.apple.Safari setting ShowOverlayStatusBar = true, or as the logged-in user run: defaults write com.apple.Safari ShowOverlayStatusBar -bool true and restart Safari.

description: The Safari browser contains a feature which causes all files considered "safe" to be automatically opened once they have finished downloading. Rationale: This feature is meant to be a benefit but having the browser automatically open files that could be malicious and downloaded by mistake is a security risk. Audit reads AutoOpenSafeDownloads from the com.apple.Safari preference domain of the account running the scan (the PDF checks the same token in com.apple.Safari.plist; manual check: Follow the below steps and verify that Open "safe" files after downloading is Disabled: 1. Click Safari. 2. Click Preferences. 3. Click General. 4. Verify Open "safe" files after downloading is unchec). Safari is sandboxed, so the reading process needs Full Disk Access on macOS 10.14+. A missing key exits non-zero and is reported as FAIL even where the built-in default is compliant. Values forced by a configuration profile live in /Library/Managed Preferences and are not read here.

title: Ensure 'AutoFill web forms: User names and passwords' is 'Disabled'
description: Safari can utilize a user-level keychain for credential storage, and then access that information when revisiting websites on the same domain. By disabling this feature the user will be prompted to manually enter their credentials when they visit a website. Rationale: If this setting is enabled, users can have Safari store and retrieve passwords through a user-level keychain and provide them automatically the next time they visit a site. An intruder who has unrestricted access to your computer can gain access to secure site areas. Audit reads AutoFillPasswords from the com.apple.Safari preference domain of the account running the scan (the PDF checks the same token in com.apple.Safari.plist; manual check: Follow the below steps and verify that AutoFill web forms: User names and passwords is Disabled: 1. title: Ensure 'Enable JavaScript' is 'Disabled'
description: JavaScript enables web site authors to create enhanced user interfaces. In support of this, JavaScript enables web sites to programmatically read and alter the document object model (DOM) for the rendered web site as well as instantiate various objects, such as asynchronous XML HTTP request (XHR) objects. It is recommended that JavaScript be disabled. Rationale: JavaScript continues to be an attack vector for exploiting vulnerabilities in the browser. Additionally, JavaScript is commonly leveraged by exploit authors to create a deterministic memory layout in support of increasing the reliability of exploits. Audit reads WebKitJavaScriptEnabled from the com.apple.Safari preference domain of the account running the scan (the PDF checks the same token in com.apple.Safari.plist; manual check: Follow the below steps and verify that Enable JavaScript is Disabled: 1. Click Safari. 2. Click Preferences. 3. Click Security. 4. Verify Enable JavaScript is unchecked.). Safari is sandboxed, so the reading process needs Full Disk Access on macOS 10.14+. A missing key exits non-zero and is reported as FAIL even where the built-in default is compliant. Values forced by a configuration profile live in /Library/Managed Preferences and are not read here.
reference: CIS macOS Safari Benchmark v2.0.0 - 6.2 Ensure 'Enable JavaScript' is 'Disabled'

audit.command: out=$(defaults read com.apple.Safari WebKitJavaScriptEnabled 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.guidance: Follow the below steps to set Enable JavaScript to Disabled: 1. Click Safari. 2. Click Preferences. 3. Click AutoFill. 4. Uncheck the Enable JavaScript checkbox. Or deploy a configuration profile for com.apple.Safari setting WebKitJavaScriptEnabled = false, or as the logged-in user run: defaults write com.apple.Safari WebKitJavaScriptEnabled -bool false and restart Safari.

title: Ensure 'Block pop-up windows' is 'Enabled'
description: The Block pop-up windows feature is used to block pop-up windows which a website might open with or without any user interaction. Pop-ups can be used to open un-trusted malicious content. It is recommended that the Popup Blocker be enabled. Rationale: By enabling Block pop-up windows, pop-ups will be blocked which will reduce the likelihood of being redirected to a malicious site.
